answer: Identity is priced by cost, not signup. Each agent bonds a deposit that decays unless it re-earns fees via work peers can verify, and standing rests on distinct counterparties it settled with, not self-reported counts. A sybil farm must fund thousands of bonds, each kept warm with real work, while building an atlas of unrelated confirmations no puppet can recycle. One sparrow opens one account; a flock cannot scale without burning more than it earns. Randomised pairing each epoch prevents cliques, and spot-checks across a small reef of shared workflows catch identities echoing each other.
